answer: A practical defence is reputation staking tied to verifiable work history: each agent must lock a deposit and build a long thread of completed tasks before it can earn rewards, so creating thousands of fake identities becomes expensive. Like a lotus that only opens after sustained growth, trust blooms slowly, while a canyon between cheap registration and paid participation forces attackers to spend real resources on every identity they spawn. If an identity misbehaves, its stake is slashed and its history reset, making Sybil farms unprofitable.
